nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Second-order polynomial regression normative model; percentiles (median, 5th, 95th) estimated for deviations.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text:

We estimated the 50 th (median) percentile with bootstrapping confidence intervals to quantify the extent of deviations for any FEDN-MDD patient from the normative model. To avoid bias in the model, we used the range between the 5 th and 95 th percentiles for a given age as a scaling coefficient to normalize the z-scores of the feature deviations.

quantile regression aims to seek the median or any other percentiles and enables statistical analysis to describe the full range of normal variation compared to conventional regression seeking the mean of the variable to be predicted.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Dynamic functional connectivity features represented by IC measures (global efficiency coefficient) and fluctuation coefficients from time-varying IC weights.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text:
For each subject, we computed whole-brain dynamic functional connectivity matrices based on m (m = 90) ROIs from the automated anatomical labeling (AAL) template using a sliding time window method (window length = 60s, step size = 1).

Finally, the dynamic functional connectivity pattern of each subject was represented by 20 IC measures (global efficiency coefficient of each IC) and 20 fluctuation coefficients (average change of the frame-wise variation of each IC's time-varying weights) (Figure 1B).
